title: ID0377416-DC/Si-D/NO-[MP / P3 160373407] False emergency stop error
description:
Charger does not have emergency stop button.
This happens random on this charger but maybe once every 2 weeks.
Several reboots often fixes the issue.
See picture from HMI
Reported behavior/issue:
False emergency stop error
Root cause:
PLC head and base unit module not connected properly
Solution:
There is a poor connection between the PLC and the modules KF2 to KF9
.
On DAMEX Sanctioned List:
Warranty Status: 8/7/2023

additional_info.subject: RE: 0377416 - ID0377411-DC/Si-D/NO-[MP / P3 160373407] False emergency stop error CRM:02023000116
additional_info.body:
Hello Simen Aarre,
We recommend you follow the below steps to troubleshoot the issue.
Trace the 24V Source:
Start from the QA26 input and trace the 24V power supply path backwards through the circuit.
Identify the origin of the 24V supply by examining each component and connection from the end point (QA26) to its source.
Component Examination:
Focus on the FA7 and FA8 components to determine their role in supplying 24V to QA26.
Verify the functionality of FA7 and FA8 to ensure they are operating correctly and supplying the required voltage
Voltage Check at XD34:19A:
Measure the voltage at XD34:19A.
If 24V is present at XD34:19A, this indicates that the sensors are closed, which implies that the doors are open.
If 24V is not present at XD34:19A, investigate potential issues with FA7 and FA8, as they may be causing the problem.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Vikas Khiladkar

additional_info.subject: Troubleshooting on site 2024-09-18
additional_info.body: We checked the complete chain off emergency stop and found nothing wrong. We checked the QA26 and same there, nothing wrong. We then checked the plc and it modules. The technincan on site found a bad connection between the plc and the modules KF2…KF9. He fixed it and did a reboot. After that the error disappered.
